messages:
Oncall-Bot: SEV2 alert - kv-cache resident on gpu-node-12 rising steadily for ~48h, OOM risk. auto-escalate to eng-oncall. Links: https://metrics/redwood/kv-cache/gpu-node-12 :rotating_light:
Maya R: Acked. I’m oncall. starting triage. pulling last 24h heap and kv page counts now.
Jordan L: FYI saw small uptick last week on same node cluster, maybe related to paged-attention allocator fragmentation.
Maya R: kubectl top nodes shows gpu-node-12 memory 98% used, pods runtime-123, runtime-124 on that node. Running `kubectl describe pod runtime-123 -n runtime` now.
Samir: getting repeated cuda errors in logs around 03:42 UTC: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` then container restart. paste logs: ```stderr
[2026-02-12T03:42:10Z] ERROR: allocator: failed to allocate kv page: out of memory
[2026-02-12T03:42:11Z] WARN: paging: fragmented pages=17289 compactable=512
```
Carla P: (reacted :eyes:) Customers on p99 latency spike ~2-3s on embeddings and a few 500s. CS has one customer reporting retries.
Maya R: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon gpu-node-12, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) scale up a replacement node, 4) canary restart one runtime pod with `KV_PAGE_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.6` and `KV_EVICT_RATE=0.05`.
Ops Lead: +1. prioritize low-impact drain first, leave one runtime pod to validate canary. Notify infra.
Infra-Bot: cordon gpu-node-12 issued by Maya R at 03:50 UTC. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` succeeded.
Jordan L: quick sanity: run `pmap` style memory map inside container to spot resident leak. also dumping allocator histogram to S3: `s3://redwood-debug/kv-hist/1732104567`
Maya R: canary restart runtime-123 with env overrides now. `kubectl set env pod/runtime-123 KV_PAGE_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=0.6 KV_EVICT_RATE=0.05 -n runtime` then rolling restart.
Samir: after canary restart, KV resident dropped ~22% on that pod within 2 minutes. metric: `kv_resident_bytes` for runtime-123 down from 78GB -> 61GB. promising.
Carla P: customer impact reduced - error spikes stopped, p99 improving. Notifying affected customers: pinged CS to send update.
Maya R: draining node in progress - moving batch of non-critical pods off node. scaling up replacement node group to absorb load.
Jordan L: observed allocator compaction logs during canary: `compact: freed_pages=1400 reclaimed=3.2GB fragmentation=0.12`. Looks like fragmentation high and compaction effective.
Maya R: plan for next 24h: 1) apply env tweak cluster-wide for affected runtime pools, 2) run background compaction cron for 6 hours, 3) add eviction telemetry alert earlier, 4) postmortem.
Ops Lead: agree. Add short-term config push to Dedicated pools only. We need safety: if compaction spikes CPU, auto-fallback to previous thresholds.
Samir: opened internal ticket INF-5421 to track RCA (kv allocator slow creep -> fragmentation -> OOM). Assigning Jordan + Maya. Will include heap dumps and kernel cgroup traces.
Maya R: walkthrough notes for handoff: node cordoned, replacement nodes added, canary showing immediate improvement, customer impact mitigated. handing off to next oncall at 07:00 UTC. Please continue monitoring kv_resident, cuda OOM errors, container restarts.
Oncall-Bot: Handoff reminder: next oncall @Jordan L from 07:00 UTC. Paging window extended 6h.
Jordan L: Received handoff. Will run broader rollout at 07:30 if metrics hold. Also will add a short-lived eviction pressure test on staging to reproduce.
Carla P: Filing customer update: brief summary + ETA for follow-up postmortem. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
Maya R: Thanks everyone. Postmortem notes: candidate root cause = slow leak from paged-attention allocator plus high fragmentation on long-lived KV pages. Long-term: allocator defrag improvements + auto-compaction + earlier alerting on compactable page ratio.
Infra-Bot: Created incident ticket INC-1732104567 and linked logs.
Maya R: closing thread for now. If new OOMs appear, re-open and escalate.
